content:
The image shows two corn ears with a striking blue-gray to silvery-blue powdery/dusty coating covering most of the kernels. The husks are pulled back, revealing the ears. The coloration is a distinctive dark blue-green to gray-blue, which matches the description of Trichoderma ear rot — specifically the "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels" and the coverage "from base to middle of cob covering all kernels."

Key visual evidence:
- Two exposed corn ears with husks pulled back
- Kernels covered in a pervasive blue-gray to gray-green powdery/conidial layer
- The coating appears dense and covers most of the ear surface
- Some orange/yellow healthy kernels still visible beneath, suggesting the mold is overlaying the kernels
- The blue-gray color is characteristic of Trichoderma conidia, not the olive-green of Aspergillus or pink of Fusarium
